heroHeadline: Halane Talks Collapse — T-2 Days to Constitutional Deadline; Opposition, Government Fail to Bridge Election Deadlock; Thursday Talks Last Chance
heroSubtitle: Somalia's political crisis hit a critical inflection on May 13, 2026 — two days before President Mohamud's May 15 constitutional deadline — as the long-disputed Halane compound talks finally took place but collapsed without any agreement. President Mohamud and Deputy PM Salah Ahmed Jama faced former President Sharif Sheikh Ahmed and Puntland's Saeed Abdullahi Deni; the opposition opened by demanding release of political detainees (which Mohamud accepted), but talks broke down over the electoral framework — the government proposed technical committees, which the opposition rejected as a stalling tactic. A final negotiating session is scheduled for Thursday, May 14. The collapse deepens the path to the May 16 opposition protest (the day after the deadline), which the opposition announced would proceed regardless. The World Bank simultaneously released its Somalia Economic Update warning GDP growth slowed to 3% in 2025 and is projected at 2.8% in 2026, with aid cuts and piracy compounding structural risks. All three pirate-held vessels remain captive: Honour 25 (Day 18), Sward (Day 17), MT Eureka (Day 11) — 44 hostages total. WFP's July 2026 shutdown warning remains in effect: 6M food insecure, 1.9M children malnourished, only 1 in 10 reached.
footerNote: Data sourced from ACLED, OCHA, UNSOM, WFP, AFRICOM, EU EPF, EU NAVFOR, Combined Maritime Forces, UN Monitoring Group, World Bank, and major international outlets. Casualty figures contested where noted.
